transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. I'm here to help. What brings you in today?

I'm just really struggling with how awful my skin looks because of these terrible acne scars on my face. It's all I can think about, and I feel like it completely ruins my appearance. Everyone else tells me my skin looks perfectly fine, but I know they're just trying to be nice because it looks hideous to me.
How much time do you spend each day thinking about your skin or doing things like checking mirrors, touching your face, or seeking reassurance about your appearance?

I easily spend three to four hours every day constantly checking the mirror and picking at my skin to try and fix the flaws. I am also repetitively asking my family for reassurance about how I look, and this whole routine is just incredibly exhausting and distressing.
Has this concern about your skin affected your ability to work, go to school, or spend time with others?
I'm not really sure, to be honest. I haven't thought much about how it affects my work or social life because I'm just so focused on how bad my skin looks.

The patient's lack of insight into functional impairment does not rule out the disorder, as insight can be poor in this condition. final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits a preoccupation with perceived defects in appearance (acne scars) that are not observable or appear slight to others, engages in repetitive behaviors (mirror checking, skin picking, reassurance seeking), and experiences significant distress. These symptoms align with diagnostic criteria for Body Dysmorphic Disorder.
